text:
maria: Quick sanity check — following the RFC merge, we're seeing a few cases where KV cache gets evicted while a prefetch is in-flight. I want to align on the admission <-> allocator boundary so drains don't lose warm state.

alex: Are these mostly long-tail tenants or short bursts?

maria: Mostly long-tail with occasional microbursts. The problem is eviction happens during the microburst because allocator signals low headroom.

shen: My take: we need a soft-drain handshake. Allocator should expose a small TTL/lease for recently-prefetched keys so the batch can finish. Not full pinning, just a short-lived promise.

leah: +1 for lease. Also we should add a "prefetch_inflight" gauge and a rejected-prefetch counter so we can measure how often we lose warms.

alex: How would the API look? Something like: admission returns {lease_id, headroom_hint, latency_budget_ms} and allocator understands lease_id on eviction?

maria: Example sketch: ```json
{
  "lease_id": "abc123",
  "headroom_hint": 120,
  "latency_budget_ms": 80
}
```

shen: That works. Important: keep lease semantics weak — best-effort guarantee. If node truly needs memory, it can revoke but should return a reason code (e.g., OOM_PRESSURE or PREEMPT_HIGH).

leah: Also add a signal for "eviction_grace_ms" so allocator knows how long to delay kill-off. We can default to 200ms.

alex: Two concerns: 1) complexity in allocator state machine, 2) potential for headroom inflation (tenants holding tiny leases forever).

maria: For (2) we add a max-lease-per-tenant and global-lease-quota. Also leases must decay if not actively used (touch updates ttl).

shen: For (1) we should model it as a simple callback path: admission -> lease issued -> eviction attempt -> allocator checks active_leases -> if any active -> attempt soft-evict (move to swap slot) else hard-evict. Keep it event-driven, not blocking the main allocation loop.

leah: Ops question: what telemetry do we need to alert on misbehaviour? I propose: stale_lease_count, lease_revocations_per_min, prefetch_retries, and percent_warm_hits_lost.

maria: Agree. We should also add a cheap histogram for time-from-lease-issue-to-eviction to detect tight races.

alex: One more tradeoff: do we let admission request extra headroom_preference for critical paths (high-QPS tenants) vs normal? If yes, we need a priority tier on leases.

shen: We already have tenant tiers; reuse that. Higher-tier gets longer eviction_grace_ms and higher max-lease-per-tenant. Keep defaults conservative.

leah: Implementation checklist: 1) add lease proto to admission response, 2) allocator checks active_leases before eviction, 3) metrics & dashboards, 4) chaos test that simulates rapid evict/prefetch loops.

maria: I'll open a small follow-up RFC with the proto + default numbers. Can one of you pick up the allocator patch?

alex: I can take allocator side. Will prototype event-driven check and a config flag to enable soft-leases behind a kill-switch.

shen: I'll add telemetry and the chaos test to the eval harness.

deploy-bot: CI: 1748210200 - unit tests passed on runtime/allocator.

leah: Nice. If we get the chaos test results next week we can decide defaults. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — keeping this lightweight. If anyone hits odd perf regressions, @maria please ping.
